title: Correct band width
description: Essential Criteria: The final answer for part (1) must be expressed as a function of R, specifically $(1-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3})R$ or its equivalent simplified form.

title: Correct minimum angle
description: Essential Criteria: The final answer for part (2) must be $45^{\circ}$ or $\pi/4$ radians.

title: Applies Snell's Law
description: Important Criteria: The solution must correctly apply Snell's law at the curved surface to relate the incident angle θ and refractive index n to the refraction angle β.

title: Uses geometry for width
description: Important Criteria: The solution must use the geometry of the semicircle and tangents of the refraction angles to calculate the band width on the screen as R(tan β2 - tan β1).

title: Identifies critical condition
description: Important Criteria: For part (2), the solution must identify that the band becomes a single spot when the highest index light (n2) undergoes total internal reflection, or equivalently when the lowest index light (n1) is at its critical angle.

title: Calculates critical angle
description: Important Criteria: The solution must correctly calculate the critical angle for the refractive index n1 using sin C = 1/n1.

title: Unit consistency
description: Optional Criteria: The solution should handle angles consistently (degrees/radians) and ensure the width has correct units of length.

title: Misapplies Snell's Law
description: Pitfall Criteria: Penalize if Snell's law is incorrectly written (e.g., sin θ / sin β = n) or if the incident and refraction angles are swapped.

title: Confuses width formula
description: Pitfall Criteria: Penalize if the band width is incorrectly calculated, such as using R(sin β2 - sin β1) or R(β2 - β1) instead of the correct difference in tangents.

title: Wrong critical index
description: Pitfall Criteria: Penalize if the condition for a single spot is incorrectly based on the critical angle for n2 instead of n1, leading to an answer like arcsin(1/√3).
